properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): nothing served can say which of N texts the design already holds, read-only or in one call. The server's only normalised matcher (search_first) was built as a write-time guard at 7 constructors, and search_design returns one query's raw BM25 scores, which do not separate present items from absent ones. So a population check is done by grepping the export
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-28, triaging art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27 (dev_storyflow session 62995724, 2026-09-27, while moving the project to the hosted graph) under rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed. The companion idea is wish #47.

① OBSERVED, the reporter's words: "No way to ask 'which of these external items is already represented?' Migrating 71 memory files meant grepping the exported JSON for file names and then searching by keyword per item." EXPECTED: one call that takes the list and says, for each item, what the design already holds. NOT AFFECTED: looking up a single item works. search_design ranks every node type, and the same report praises it for finding a ruling recorded as a Decision, Requirement or Constraint rather than as a rule.

② PRECEDENT (search_design on the raw words): no earlier record of a batch or read-only "is this already here?" check. The nearest records are:
· cap:search-first-at-the-tool, the write-time near-match guard.
· fact:the-near-match-guard-shows-three-of-a-nine-way-tie-so-relevance-is-decided-by-score-noise.
· dec:idea-what-gets-searched-repeatedly-is-becoming-important, which holds the design's own measurement that BM25 scores are not comparable across queries (the same topic scored 4.48 and 35.75).
· dec:idea-a-bulk-write-can-be-checked-before-it-is-written (check_only, since built).
· fact:the-served-instructions-name-no-way-to-ask-whether-a-thing-already-exists-and-one-consumer-rebuilt-four-that-did. That one is about whether a TOOL exists, not whether a node does: a different class.

③ CANDIDATES:
(A) MISSING TOOL. No served matcher exists, batch or read-only.
(B) DISCOVERABILITY. One exists and was not found: ingest_corpus_step (N documents, dedupe across documents), relation_candidates, create_nodes check_only, or the near-match guard.
(C) ALLOCATION. The one normalised matcher the server has lives only inside the write path.
(D) SCORE MEANING. Even a batch wrapper over search_design could not return a per-item score anyone could trust.
(E) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG. Searching item by item is cheap enough that batching buys nothing.

④ WHAT WOULD SEPARATE THEM: B predicts a served tool that takes external text in bulk and reports existing matches without writing. E predicts that per-call cost is mostly server compute. D predicts that a present item's own paraphrase can score below an absent item's best hit.

⑤ RESULTS, using the 0.72.0 binary on a scratch copy of reflow2's export (5,668 nodes):
· search_design takes a single `query` (default limit 10), and no read tool takes a list of queries. A one-shot search_design took 0.69–0.79 s, against 0.69–0.88 s for a no-op design_identity, so the search itself costs next to nothing. 71 items means 71 round trips and 71 results to read.
· find_tools for "is this already in the graph", "which of these items is already represented", "match a list of texts against the design", "search many phrases at once" and "find duplicates of a list of items" returned no matcher. search_design ranked first only for "search many phrases at once". find_skills returned nothing relevant.
· relation_candidates takes an EXISTING node_id, not external text.
· ingest_corpus_step is a WRITE (an extraction handshake). Its dedupe compares only the NAMES of extracted nodes against existing nodes of the same type (token_sort_ratio ≥ 70, ingest.rs fuzzy_match), so it is not a read-only check of what is represented. It is also absent from the hosted tool list (checked on the storyflow surface), and the hosted engine is where the reporter worked.
· create_nodes check_only validates the schema and nothing else. A near-verbatim copy of rule:a-finding-is-written-before-the-answer-and-needs-no-permission passed with no near-match reported.
· search_first (capture.rs) is exactly the per-item comparison the reporter asked for: a whole-design BM25 search whose baseline is the new node's OWN score, with a floor of 0.5 × that score and up to 6 hits. It runs at 7 single add_* constructor sites, only after the node is in the index, and nowhere else.
· Raw scores do not separate present items from absent ones. A paraphrase of rule:a-finding-is-written-before-the-answer-and-needs-no-permission put that rule 4th, at 20.9. A note that the design does not hold ("remote from phone cannot run restart or sign in", which exists only in an agent's memory) got a best hit of 21.3. A present fact scored 26.4, only 3.5 points ahead of rank 2.
⇒ B REFUTED: nothing served does this, so the right diagnosis is tool_missing. E REFUTED: the cost is round trips and reading results, not compute. A, C and D HOLD.

⑥ CLASS: a population check has no read-only or batch form, so it gets done by grep outside the design. The reason is that the server's only normalised "is this already here?" computation was built as a write-time guard (it needs the text in the index for its self-score baseline), and the read tool returns raw BM25 scores that cannot be compared from one item to the next. COUNTS: 1 normalised matcher, 7 write sites, 0 read tools, 0 bulk forms. Any rule that says "enumerate the population before classifying" (storyflow's rule:enumerate_the_population_before_acting_on_a_classification is one) is therefore expensive to obey on this surface, by construction.

⑦ OUT OF SCOPE; no code was changed. A test pinning the CLASS would build a list of texts in which some are verbatim or paraphrased copies of existing nodes of any type and the rest are absent. It would assert that ONE read-only call writes nothing and returns, for each text, candidate nodes with a score that can be compared ACROSS texts (for example, normalised to the text's own self-score). Every present item's source node must be among its candidates, and every absent item must get a lower normalised score. The answer for a text must also match what the write guard would report for that same text.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSION. HELD: there is no bulk matcher, and searching item by item was the only served route. QUALIFIED: "best hit + score", as asked, would mislead if the score were raw BM25 (measured above). The useful form is a list of candidates with a normalised score, and deciding whether an item is represented stays a judgement.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: storyflow's design size, and how the 71 memory files phrase things (not read). Whether search_first's 0.5 floor would separate present from absent items on memory-file prose; the self-score baseline was not replayed on these probes. Per-call latency over the network on flo2 (not measured).
